assessment:
Two wishes now, and they are not the same tool. Vampiric Tutor is {B} at instant speed for any card, taken in secret, put on top, costing two life and your next draw. Forerunner of the Legion is a {2}{W} 2/2 that finds a Vampire, REVEALS it, and puts it on top — and being a Vampire spell, casting it mints an eminence token on the way in.

Start with what Forerunner cannot do, because it decides which wish goes where. THE GO-WIDE KILL wants a token-to-damage payoff beside a multiplier. Of the seven payoffs, five fire when a creature ENTERS — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Witty Roastmaster — and not one is a Vampire. The two Forerunner can reach, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, fire when a creature DIES, which is not the event stack 009 verified. The other half of that pair holds three true doublers — Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Elspeth — and four cards that simply make extra tokens. Forerunner finds none of the doublers and three of the makers: Mavren Fein, Charismatic Conqueror, Bloodline Keeper. Stack 010 is the reason that gap is worth naming: three doublers turn one eminence trigger into eight tokens under all six application orders, and Forerunner cannot go and get the third one.

So the go-wide kill is Vampiric Tutor's job. It assembles in 49.1% of games and by turn six in 32.7%; spend the wish on it and that is 55.6% and 38.2% (◆ goldfish, 10,000 seeded games). Its third leg — a Vampire cheap enough to cast alongside the rest of the turn — is already there in 92.3% of games and 84.8% by turn six, so never spend a wish on it.

Forerunner's job is the drain lines and the bodies, and it is good at that job because both single points of failure are Vampires: Bloodthirsty Conqueror, half of the checker-passed loops in stacks 004 and 006, and Bloodletter of Aclazotz, the doubler in stack 003. So are Vito, Sanctum Seeker, Champion of Dusk. Sanguine Bond and Throne of the God-Pharaoh are not, and this search will never see them.

Two costs to say out loud before either wish. Both put the card on TOP, which is a turn of delay unless something cashes it — Herald's Horn's upkeep look hands you a Vampire creature and leaves your draw step intact, and Skullclamp, Night's Whisper, Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent, Preacher of the Schism, Champion of Dusk and Pact of the Serpent all turn a stacked top card into a card in hand. And Forerunner reveals what it takes: the blue seat learns your plan a full turn before you cast it. In the one game on record, two counters on two named cards decided the result. Vampiric Tutor reveals nothing, and that is a reason to hold it for the turn the table is representing an answer.

tutors.notes: One mana at instant speed, any card, on TOP — plus two life and your next draw. That shape dictates the timing: cast it at the end step right before your untap, when the table's mana and attention are spent, and only when you will cast the card the turn it arrives. A Vampiric cast three turns early is a card spent arranging a draw you then draw into removal range. Pay the two life without blinking — Sanctum Seeker and the lifegain halves hand it straight back. It is also the only one of the two wishes that reaches a card which is not a Vampire, so spend it on the enchantments and the artifact — Anointed Procession, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Sanguine Bond, Throne of the God-Pharaoh — and leave the Vampires to Forerunner. And it takes in secret: nothing is revealed, which is what makes it the wish to cast against a seat holding counterspells.

targets.scenario: Opponent 3's end step, turn four. You have a doubler and five bodies but no converter, three untapped lands, and your untap is next. Player 2 just tapped out for a planeswalker.
targets.why: The go-wide kill is online by turn six in 32.7% of your games on natural draws and 38.2% with a wish spent on it — this is the wish, at the moment the table cannot answer it. Roastmaster is one of the five payoffs that fire when a creature ENTERS, and none of the five is a Vampire, so Forerunner cannot go and get any of them. This half of the plan is Vampiric Tutor's alone. Roastmaster is the converter on a body: every later entry is one damage to each seat, and he triggers the other converters on his own way in. One mana at their end step, cast him on your turn with mana to spare.

citations.quote: prefer committing at the end step before your own turn so the table's chances to respond are spent

targets.scenario: The sweeper seat has held five mana across two turns and is visibly waiting. You have seven Vampires, the table knows the wipe is coming, and your hand is lands.
targets.why: Make the wipe cost them the game instead of costing you yours. With Celebrant down, every creature you lose drains each opponent for one and pays you one — seven deaths is seven off each seat while you rebuild from the command zone. Prefer him over Blood Artist when the whole table matters: Artist drains one target player per death, Celebrant hits everyone. Fetch at their end step, cast him for two, and stop being afraid of the wipe.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can

targets.scenario: Sanctum Seeker and six other Vampires are on your board, untapped, and your attack is next turn. Two opponents are at 14 and 16. You can pay {B}{B}{B} plus one.
targets.why: This is the closing fetch, and the maths is verified: stack 003 resolves a seven-Vampire attack with Bloodletter and Sanctum Seeker as 14 life off each opponent on attack declaration alone — before a single point of combat damage. Both life totals in this scenario are inside that number. The rule attached: he is the only triple-black cast in the 99, so confirm the {B}{B}{B} is actually there before the wish, not after — black is 30 sources against the 36 a 90% on-curve rate would take.

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. Opponent 2's end step. The blue seat has held two untapped Islands for three turns and has countered the last two spells anyone tried to resolve. Edgar is on the battlefield, you have six Vampires, a five-mana refuel stranded in hand, and one black source untapped.
targets.why: Do not fetch a better spell. Fetch the thing that makes the spell you are already holding resolve. Deflecting Swat changes the target of a counterspell, and with Edgar on the battlefield you cast it without paying its mana cost — so the refuel goes through and their held mana bought a redirected spell. Read the condition rather than the card: 'if you control a commander' means Edgar on the battlefield, not in the command zone, and without him the Swat costs {2}{R} and belongs to a different turn. Vampiric Tutor reveals nothing on its way through, so the seat you are answering cannot see the answer coming. In the one game on record, two counters on named cards decided the result.

citations.quote: sequence so one removal spell can't break the chain

tutors.notes: {2}{W} for a 2/2, and three things happen on one cast. It is a Vampire spell, so eminence mints a 1/1 token — stack 010 is checker-passed that eminence works with Edgar in the command zone and never on the battlefield. The body arrives. And its enter trigger searches out a Vampire card and puts it on top. White is 22 sources against a 22-source yardstick, so unlike the deck's black costs it casts on curve. Two limits govern every fetch below and neither goes away. The search is Vampire-only, which is most of the go-wide kill out of reach: of the seven token-to-damage payoffs it can find two, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, and of the seven cards in the multiplier-or-extra-token-maker group it can find three — Mavren Fein, Charismatic Conqueror, Bloodline Keeper — every one of which makes an extra token rather than doubling one. The three that actually double (Anointed Procession, Mondrak, Elspeth) are all out of reach. And it REVEALS what it takes, so the table sees the card a full turn before you cast it. Fetch what you want NEXT turn, not this one — unless Herald's Horn is out with Vampire named, in which case the upkeep look puts the card in hand and your draw step still draws. Its second ability is small and real: every later Vampire that enters, tokens included, pumps a creature of your choice until end of turn.

targets.scenario: Turn three, Forerunner is the play. You have two bodies — which is where the goldfish has you on turn three, mean 2.058 — no converter on the battlefield, and all three opponents untapped and above 30.
targets.why: Buy the conversion Forerunner can actually reach. Five of the seven token-to-damage payoffs fire when a creature ENTERS — Purphoros, Impact Tremors, Warleader's Call, Corpse Knight, Witty Roastmaster — and not one of them is a Vampire, so this search cannot see them. The two it can see, Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant, fire when a creature DIES, which is not the line stack 009 verified. What is left is combat, and Sanctum Seeker is the card that turns width into damage there: each attacking Vampire drains every opponent for one. Stack 003 measured that at width — seven attackers is seven triggers, and with Bloodletter of Aclazotz out it is 14 life off each opponent on attack declaration, before blockers are declared. The life it hands back is also the input Vito and Sanguine Bond convert.

citations.quote: Your cards should do something to all three seats or win the game

targets.scenario: The behind fetch. The turn after the second sweeper. You have three lands, Forerunner in hand, Edgar back in the command zone, and the blue seat still has two untapped Islands. After you cast Forerunner your hand is one land.
targets.why: Rebuild into a drip rather than a refill. Welcoming Vampire draws a card whenever one or more other creatures with power 2 or less enter, once each turn — and every eminence token is a 1/1, so the plan you are already running becomes a card a turn from a three-mana body. A draw engine is drawn in 73.3% of games and by turn six in 62.1%, so a third of your games ask you to go and get one, and Forerunner can reach exactly two: this and Champion of Dusk. Take this one into open blue mana. Champion is five mana and one large refill — the shape a held counterspell most wants to meet — while Welcoming Vampire costs a seat's counter to stop one card and then you cast another Vampire.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can

targets.scenario: The closing fetch. Turn six or later. Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose is on the battlefield and untouched, you have five lands untapped after Forerunner, and nobody at the table has shown blue mana this game.
targets.why: The one fetch that ends the game instead of improving it. Stack 004 is checker-passed: Conqueror beside Vito is a deterministic table kill from a three-life seed — 13 Vito resolutions, both opponents to exactly zero, and the loop consumes no cards, mana or creatures. Stack 006 proves the same pairing with Sanguine Bond in Vito's place, and Forerunner can find the Conqueror half and the Vito half and never Sanguine Bond, which is an enchantment. Price two things before you take it. He costs {3}{B}{B} and lands the turn AFTER the search, and he is a 5/5 creature, so every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed creature removal — stack 004 names that cost itself. Then there is the reveal, which tells the table which card is coming while it is still on top of your library. The loop assembles in 4.6% of games and 10.2% with a wish, so carry the ticket and never steer for it.

targets.scenario: The wish nobody sees coming. Turn three. Bloodletter of Aclazotz and Champion of Dusk are both in hand, your three lands produce exactly one black between them, and a spare eminence token is on the battlefield.
targets.why: Fetch the mana, not the threat. Master of Dark Rites is a one-mana 1/1 that taps and sacrifices another creature for {B}{B}{B}, and eminence prints the creature to sacrifice on every Vampire spell you cast. Black is 30 sources against the 36 a 90% on-curve rate would take, and Bloodletter of Aclazotz is the only triple-black cast in the 99, so this is the card that makes the deck's most expensive coloured cost payable a turn early. The restriction is exact, and deck-facts names it: that mana pays for Vampire, Cleric and Demon SPELLS, and an activated ability is not a spell. It casts Bloodletter (Vampire Demon), Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Champion of Dusk (Vampire Knights) and Vito (Vampire Cleric); it cannot pay Vito's own {3}{B}{B} lifelink activation or Indulgent Aristocrat's {2}, and Sanguine Bond is an enchantment and out of reach. Bank the free part: the token you sacrifice is a creature dying, so Cruel Celebrant, Blood Artist and Cordial Vampire all fire off the cost.

gaps: The goldfish models only UNRESTRICTED tutors as wildcards ('search your library for a card'), so every *_assisted figure quoted here is Vampiric Tutor alone. Forerunner of the Legion is priced at zero in every measurement of this deck — goldfish_targets.json says so in its own note, and the model has no way to represent a Vampire-only search. The assisted figures are therefore a ceiling on Vampiric Tutor (its top-of-library lag and two life are not modelled) and a floor on the pair.

A caveat on reading one group's rate as the plan's rate, and it lands exactly where Forerunner reaches. goldfish_targets.json's TOKEN -> DAMAGE group holds seven cards, and two of them — Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant — trigger on a creature DYING rather than entering. Both genuinely convert tokens into damage, so the group is not wrong; but stack 009's verified nine-trigger line is an ENTRY line, and a fetch into the death half does not reproduce it. Those two are the only members of that group Forerunner can find.

Nothing simulates opposing interaction, so every fetch-versus-hold call here — and the whole cost of Forerunner's reveal — is coaching judgment on top of measured assembly rates. The one logged game had two named cards countered by the same seat; one game is an anecdote, not a rate, and no artifact measures what a revealed fetch costs.

There is no graveyard answer in the 99 to fetch: confirmed at the oracle level across all 96 entries, where the only cards naming a graveyard are Takenuma, Abandoned Mire (your own) and Nighthawk Scavenger (a power count). Against a reanimator seat these two tutors buy speed, never an answer. A tutor cannot buy a class the deck does not hold.
